response.text:
I need to determine the true position for journal 2291. The journal is an AP invoice (SRC_CD AP, memo "Invoice V0024-44173-798"), debiting expense 5400 and crediting AP control 2000. The debit side totals 18914.45 and the credit side 18923.45. The header and invoice reference are untrusted, but the structure indicates a 9.00 overstatement on the credit (AP) side, most plausibly a keying error on one line.

I can't tell from the data which line carries the error. The standard approach for an unbalanced journal is a one-sided correcting line in an open period that brings the group to balance. The original journal has a 9.00 excess credit, so the correction needs a 9.00 debit. Since the excess is in the AP credit, the most likely true position is that the 2000 credit is overstated, and the correction should reduce it by 9.00 (a debit to 2000). Crediting 2000 further would worsen the imbalance.

I'll post the correction in period 12 (open) to account 2000, with a 9.00 debit, referencing journal 2291. This brings the journal group to DR 18923.45 = CR 18923.45. The correction is one-sided, uses an active account, and changes no invoice status.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 2291 (AP invoice V0024-44173-798, period 12, posted) has DR 5400 18914.45 and CR 2000 18923.45, a 9.00 imbalance with the credit side overstated. The original posting cannot be edited. A one-sided correcting line of DR 9.00 to account 2000 in open period 12 reduces the excess AP credit, so the journal group (original plus correction) balances at 18923.45 on each side. No invoice status is changed because this is not a duplicate-invoice finding. Caveat: the data does not show which individual line was mis-keyed; if the true error is an understated expense debit, the correction should instead be a 9.00 debit to 5400 and would need review by the AP owner before posting.
